target_customer: Hardware startups and electronics makers in Europe that need fast, instant-quote PCB assembly
problem: Prototype and low-volume PCBA in Europe is slow and quoting is manual. Tenet is building an AI and robotics factory in Munich for instant-quote, fast-turnaround assembly.
business_model: Electronics manufacturing services, per-order PCBA revenue

founders.name: Emil Falk
education: Stockholm School of Economics, dropped out
previous_startups: Hardware startup with an exit (not named on YC page)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he grew up in a machining shop in Sweden.

founders.name: Fabian Andersson
founders.background_notes: Built firmware and hardware for rockets and guidance systems at an unnamed employer.

competitors.name: MacroFab
competitors.what: Online PCB assembly with automated quoting from Gerber, BOM files

competitors.name: CircuitHub
competitors.what: PCB assembly marketplace with instant quotes
competitors.funding_then: Series A announced earlier per its blog

competitors.name: JLCPCB and NextPCB
competitors.what: Low-cost Asian instant-quote prototype and assembly services
competitors.traction_then: listed in a 2026 roundup of instant-quote services

technical_complexity.rationale: Building a robotic, AI-run PCBA factory needs hardware, process engineering and capital equipment; a three-person team has to do it in Munich.

defensibility.rationale: A European local-production factory has logistics and supply-chain advantages over Asian competitors, but the process itself is replicable by well-funded rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early; established US platforms have not built a European AI factory per sources found.

market_need_then: Europe depends on Asian electronics supply; a 2026 trade article argues Europe lacks a physical manufacturing foundation, and instant-quote services exist mainly offshore or in the US.

identity.visual_style: Minimal text-based site with Made in Europe label

brand_strength.rationale: Generic name shared with a design agency and branding firms; no press about the brand found.

outcome_analysis: Tenet Industries joined YC in Spring 2026 with Swedish hardware founders building a Munich factory. No outcome exists yet; the key risks are capital intensity of building a factory, ramping real production, and competing on price with Asian services.
notes: Conflicting sources: one search summary described a YC listing for Tenet Industries as building strike drones with Hugo Frisk as CEO and HQ in Stockholm, and aggregators (VCBacked, FundedIQ) say strike drones and a $500k pre-seed from June 2026; my fetch of the YC page and the company site show PCBA with Emil Falk as CEO. Aggregator funding is unverified and not recorded. Confidence low because competition dates are missing and funding is not found. Education from the YC page. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed of June 2026 is recorded from FundedIQ; VCBacked dates it the same and a Nordic Defence Sector article says Y Combinator invests a total of 500,000 dollars. It rests on a database plus that article.
